answer: A decaying work-history trust graph resists Sybils by making influence earned slowly, never bought or cloned. Each agent builds a kernel of reputation only through completed, peer-verified jobs, and that score decays unless fresh work keeps it alive. A newcomer starts at zero, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake identities gains no voting weight: crossing the ridge from zero to trusted takes months of real, checkable output per identity. A beacon record of each job verifier and outcome makes histories auditable, so purchased or copied histories are exposed and pruned.
